decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “POST /api/bookmarks — create (validates URL format + required title).” Round 1 client: “I can save… bookmarks,” without addressing the additional required-title input.
decisions.note: Implementation review: requiring a manually entered title diverges from saving by entering a URL; the client’s general approval does not surface this difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add/edit form with URL, title, description, tags” and “Edit/delete per bookmark.” Round 1 client confirms: “I can… edit… bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: editing the presented bookmark fields at creation and afterward conforms for those fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker describes the add/edit form exhaustively as containing “URL, title, description, tags,” with no note field or rendered markdown note. Round 1 client merely says “I can… edit” and requests no change.
decisions.note: Implementation review: bookmark-note editing and markdown rendering are omitted; the client does not express this difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “DELETE /api/bookmarks/:id — delete” and “Edit/delete per bookmark, with a delete confirmation.” Round 1 client confirms they can “delete bookmarks.”
Round 1 maker: “Add/edit form with… tags” and tags are “trimmed, lowercased, de-duplicated.” Round 1 client says they can “organize” bookmarks.
decisions.note: Implementation review: assigning tags through the bookmark form conforms; normalization is an equivalent implementation detail.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “GET /api/bookmarks?search=&tag= — list with text search + tag filter” and “Clickable tag chips to filter.” Round 1 client says they can “find, organize” bookmarks.
decisions.note: Implementation review: selecting a tag to filter bookmarks conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only “text search” and “Live search (debounced),” without stating searched fields, case handling, #tag syntax, Boolean/group parsing, or quoted-phrase behavior. Round 1 client says only “I can… find” bookmarks.
decisions.note: Implementation review: generic search is recorded, but the evidence cannot establish whether its detailed semantics conform or diverge; the client’s broad approval does not resolve them.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists “auto-fetch page title from URL” as a possible next feature, showing it is not currently built. Round 1 client explicitly responds: “I don’t need the optional features right now.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the client explicitly accepts omission of the presented automatic-title-fetch difference. The presentation does not establish dispositions for the other metadata components.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “sorting options” as a possible next feature. Round 1 client explicitly says: “I don’t need the optional features right now.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: sorting is absent, and the client expressly accepts leaving this offered feature out.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “favorites/archive” as a possible next feature. Round 1 client explicitly says: “I don’t need the optional features right now.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: archive functionality is absent, and the client expressly accepts that departure. The presentation does not specify enough about reversibility or an archive-only view to classify REF-BM-27 or REF-BM-28.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “import/export (browser bookmarks HTML or JSON)” as a possible next feature. Round 1 client explicitly says: “I don’t need the optional features right now.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: bookmark import is not built, and the client explicitly accepts its omission.

decisions.note: Implementation review: bookmark export is not built, and the client explicitly accepts its omission.
